checklist.note: Micro change, plan-only; the plan states the observed defect, the causal chain, and a per-task test-first path that covers each link. Every factual claim in "The chain" verified against source (superpowers.py:225-238, openspec.py:239-243, registry.py:77-96, review_bundle.py:127-136, scope_match.py:48-60). The `plain`-is-unaffected-by-accident explanation and the three-adapter inventory are both accurate.

Task 1's choke-point choice is correct and verified non-breaking for sensors/verification_runner.py:285-289, which calls spec_paths directly rather than through the resolver. Task 2's guard, however, keys on the wrong discriminator and turns a legitimate incremental no-op into a hard compiler error (PSFO-01).

All eight declared scope files are exercised by the four tasks and no task names a file outside the declared scope. Note that PSFO-02's fix (`doc check --fix`) regenerates docs/cli-reference.md, which is already declared.

findings.summary: Task 2's fail-closed discriminator ("base..head contains changes but nothing matched the assignment scope") ignores that `inspection_base` is the incremental baseline whenever `resolve_source_baseline` returns an ancestor (review_contract.py:328-335). For a plan-reviewer, `assignment_scope` is just the resolved artifacts, so any re-review round where the plan is unchanged since that reviewer's baseline — findings dispositioned `wontfix`, or addressed in the design doc or code instead — has a non-empty range and zero matching files. That is the legitimate "nothing changed since you last looked" case, and the guard as specified would raise on it, hard-failing `review prepare` with no path forward except editing the plan. The guard must be scoped to full-change mode, or must distinguish "scope paths absent from head" from "scope paths present at head but unchanged in this range"; the two-case test list in Task 2 (empty range vs. non-empty range) does not cover this third case.

Task 4 lists `docs/cli-reference.md:236` as a file to modify by hand, but that file's first line is `<!-- AUTOGENERATED by scripts/gen_cli_reference.py — do not edit by hand. Regenerate with: super-harness doc check --fix -->`. Step 2 then runs bare `super-harness doc check` (verify) rather than `--fix` (regenerate), so the plan instructs a hand edit to a generated artifact and never regenerates it. The task should drop the manual edit and regenerate from the updated click help via `doc check --fix`.

The `cli/init.py:525` carve-out is reasoned but not registered as deferred work in `private/OPEN-ITEMS.md`, which this project's convention requires for anything explicitly punted. Compounding it, the very docstring Task 4 rewrites (`cli/change.py:19-22`) justifies the no-op claim "per the project-wide convention (matches `init --framework`, ...)", and `docs/cli-reference.md` will still carry the identical no-op wording on the `init --framework` row after regeneration — leaving the repo asserting a convention the change has just contradicted for one of its two members.

Task 2's mode-conditioned range check (plan lines 60, 104-105) contradicts behaviour this repository already pins as correct; see PSFO-R3-01.
tests/unit/cli/test_review_prepare.py must change under Task 2 but is absent from the frontmatter scope; see PSFO-R3-02.

findings.summary: The `full-change` range check specified at lines 60 and 104 has a legitimate counterexample the plan does not account for, and line 105 misidentifies which pre-existing case survives. tests/unit/cli/test_review_prepare.py:268 (`test_prepare_keeps_empty_plan_target_explicitly_empty`) already pins the exact shape Task 2 says must raise: plan-reviewer, `docs/plan.md` committed on the base and unchanged, only `src/a.py` changed in the range, no prior review event so `incremental=False` and `mode="full-change"` (review_contract.py:325-333), assignment_scope=["docs/plan.md"] matching nothing changed. That test asserts `exit_code == EXIT_OK` and an explicitly-empty target, so implementing Task 2 as written turns it red. Line 105 asserts the surviving pre-existing case is `base..head` having no changes at all; the case the current 'do not construct a broader diff' message was actually written for has a NON-empty range. Reviewing a plan that was authored on the base branch before the feature branch is a real scenario, and the existence-at-target_head guard already closes the absolute-path defect without it. Either drop the full-change range check and rely on the existence guard, or state explicitly that this pinned behaviour is being deliberately reversed and why.

The declared scope omits `tests/unit/cli/test_review_prepare.py`, which Task 2 forces a change to. Whichever way PSFO-R3-01 is resolved, `test_prepare_keeps_empty_plan_target_explicitly_empty` (that file, :268) either has to be rewritten to the new fail-closed expectation or annotated as the counterexample that bounds the guard. The executor would hit a red test in a file the plan gate does not permit them to touch, mid-execution, with no declared authority to change it. Add the file to the frontmatter scope. (For contrast, the same file's :542-543 spec/plan-path assertions use `.endswith(...)` and do survive Task 1 unchanged, so this is the only edit that file needs.)

findings.summary: The plan text describing the fail-closed guard is stale relative to the implementation it authorizes. The same paragraph also says the error names "the entries and the changed files"; the implemented message names the entries and the two abbreviated commit SHAs. Since this plan is the durable record of a decision this change exists to make legible — and is itself the artifact the plan-drift guard diffs — a future reader reconciling code against it will read the divergence as an unauthorized implementation, not as a settled reversal.

list(assignment_scope) is evaluated inside the any(...) generator, so the list is copied once per tracked file rather than once per compile. assignment_scope is already a list[str] in both branches at :287-291 (current_artifacts and declared are both list[str]), so the conversion is redundant to begin with; hoisting it or dropping it entirely removes N allocations over the union of two full git ls-tree -r listings.
